questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: identify the correct tone for a syllable
questions.stem: Which tone mark corresponds to a high level tone that stays flat?

options.text: The first tone, marked with a macron
The second tone, marked with an acute accent
options.misconception: confuses a rising tone with a level tone

options.text: The third tone, marked with a caron
options.misconception: confuses a dipping tone with a level tone

options.text: The fourth tone, marked with a grave accent
options.misconception: confuses a falling tone with a level tone

questions.explanation: The first tone is high and level, written with a macron over the vowel. The second tone rises, the third dips and rises, and the fourth falls sharply, so each distractor names a real tone applied to the wrong contour.
questions.hint: Which contour stays flat and high?

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.stem: Which tone mark rises from mid to high?

options.text: The second tone, marked with an acute accent
The first tone, marked with a macron
options.misconception: confuses a level tone with a rising tone

options.text: The third tone, marked with a caron
options.misconception: confuses a dipping tone with a rising tone

options.text: The fourth tone, marked with a grave accent
options.misconception: confuses a falling tone with a rising tone

questions.explanation: The second tone rises from mid to high and is written with an acute accent. The other marks describe different contours, so they cannot be the rising tone.
questions.hint: Which accent points upward?

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.stem: Which tone mark falls sharply from high to low?

options.text: The fourth tone, marked with a grave accent
The first tone, marked with a macron
options.misconception: confuses a level tone with a falling tone

options.text: The second tone, marked with an acute accent
options.misconception: confuses a rising tone with a falling tone

options.text: The third tone, marked with a caron
options.misconception: confuses a dipping tone with a falling tone

questions.explanation: The fourth tone falls sharply from high to low and is written with a grave accent. The other tones do not fall, so each distractor is a wrong contour.
questions.hint: Which accent points downward?

provenance.author: bank-team-ch3

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.stem: Which tone dips down and then rises again?

options.text: The third tone, marked with a caron
The first tone, marked with a macron
options.misconception: confuses a level tone with a dipping tone

options.text: The second tone, marked with an acute accent
options.misconception: confuses a rising tone with a dipping tone

options.text: The fourth tone, marked with a grave accent
options.misconception: confuses a falling tone with a dipping tone

questions.explanation: The third tone dips to low and then rises, written with a caron. It is the only tone with this dip-and-rise contour, so the other marks are wrong.
questions.hint: Which contour goes down then up?

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: apply third tone sandhi in context
questions.stem: In the phrase for hello, the first character has third tone and the second also third tone. How is the first tone pronounced?

options.text: As a second (rising) tone before another third tone
As a full third tone with a deep dip
options.misconception: ignores third tone sandhi before another third tone

options.text: As a first (level) tone before another third tone
options.misconception: applies first tone sandhi instead of second tone

options.text: As a fourth (falling) tone before another third tone
options.misconception: applies falling contour instead of rising

questions.explanation: When two third tones appear together, the first becomes a rising second tone. Pronouncing it as a full third tone or another tone breaks the natural flow.
questions.hint: What happens when two dipping tones meet?

provenance.author: bank-team-ch3
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: apply bu tone sandhi before fourth tone
questions.stem: The negation word bu normally has fourth tone. When it precedes another fourth tone word, how is bu pronounced?

options.text: As a second (rising) tone before a fourth tone
As a fourth (falling) tone before a fourth tone
options.misconception: keeps original tone instead of sandhi

options.text: As a first (level) tone before a fourth tone
options.misconception: applies wrong sandhi contour

options.text: As a third (dipping) tone before a fourth tone
options.misconception: confuses sandhi with third tone

questions.explanation: bu changes from fourth to second tone before another fourth tone. Keeping it fourth or choosing another tone produces an unnatural pronunciation.
questions.hint: Does bu rise or fall before a falling tone?

provenance.author: bank-team-ch3
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: apply yi tone sandhi before fourth tone
questions.stem: The number one yi normally has first tone. When it precedes a fourth tone word, how is yi pronounced?

options.text: As a fourth (falling) tone before a fourth tone
As a first (level) tone before a fourth tone
options.misconception: keeps original tone instead of sandhi

options.text: As a second (rising) tone before a fourth tone
options.misconception: applies bu sandhi rule instead of yi rule

options.text: As a third (dipping) tone before a fourth tone
options.misconception: confuses sandhi with third tone

questions.explanation: yi changes from first to fourth tone before a fourth tone word. Keeping it first or applying another sandhi rule is incorrect.
questions.hint: Which tone does yi take before a falling tone?

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.stem: Which statement about the neutral tone is correct?

options.text: It is light and short with no tone mark
It is high and level like the first tone
options.misconception: confuses neutral tone with first tone

options.text: It rises sharply like the second tone
options.misconception: confuses neutral tone with second tone

options.text: It falls sharply like the fourth tone
options.misconception: confuses neutral tone with fourth tone

questions.explanation: The neutral tone is light and short and carries no tone mark. The other options describe full tones, not the unstressed neutral syllable.
questions.hint: Which tone has no mark and sounds light?

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.stem: Which letter group is a valid pinyin initial consonant?

options.text: zh is a valid pinyin initial
v is a valid pinyin initial
options.misconception: v is not a standard pinyin initial

options.text: fj is a valid pinyin initial
options.misconception: fj is not a single initial

options.text: wq is a valid pinyin initial
options.misconception: wq is not a single initial

questions.explanation: zh is a standard pinyin initial consonant. v is not used as an initial, and fj or wq are not valid single initials in pinyin.
questions.hint: Which option is a real initial and not a combo?

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.stem: Which group is a valid pinyin final (vowel ending)?

options.text: iang is a valid pinyin final
yng is a valid pinyin final
options.misconception: yng is not a standard final

options.text: uei is a valid pinyin final
options.misconception: uei is not written as a final form

options.text: iou is a valid pinyin final
options.misconception: iou is not written as a final form

questions.explanation: iang is a standard pinyin final. The written forms yng, uei, and iou do not appear as finals in standard pinyin spelling.
questions.hint: Which ending is a standard final?

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: distinguish nasal finals n and ng
questions.stem: Which pair differs only by the nasal final n versus ng?

options.text: an versus ang differ by n versus ng
en versus eng differ by vowel quality
options.misconception: misattributes the difference to vowels

options.text: in versus ing differ by tone only
options.misconception: misattributes the difference to tone

options.text: un versus ung differ by initial only
options.misconception: misattributes the difference to initial

questions.explanation: an and ang differ only in the nasal final: alveolar n versus velar ng. The other pairs misstate where the difference lies.
questions.hint: Which pair changes only the nasal ending?

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.stem: Which initial is retroflex (curled tongue)?

options.text: zh is a retroflex initial
z is a retroflex initial
options.misconception: confuses flat tongue z with retroflex zh

options.text: c is a retroflex initial
options.misconception: confuses flat tongue c with retroflex ch

options.text: s is a retroflex initial
options.misconception: confuses flat tongue s with retroflex sh

questions.explanation: zh is a retroflex initial produced with a curled tongue. z, c, and s are flat-tongue initials and are not retroflex.
questions.hint: Which initial needs a curled tongue?

questions.stem: How many tones are there in standard Mandarin including the neutral tone?
questions.explanation: Standard Mandarin has four main tones plus a neutral tone, making five in total.
questions.hint: Count the four main tones plus the light one.

The water radical on the left side

Fire or heat related meaning

questions.stem: Which statement about simplified and traditional Chinese is correct?

options.text: Simplified characters have fewer strokes in many cases
Traditional characters are always shorter to write
options.misconception: reverses the stroke relationship

options.text: Simplified characters are only used in speech
options.misconception: confuses script with speech

options.text: Traditional characters have no radicals
options.misconception: false claim about radicals

questions.explanation: Simplified characters reduce stroke count in many cases compared to traditional forms. Traditional forms retain more strokes, and both use radicals.

questions.stem: In many characters, the radical indicating meaning is usually placed where?

options.text: On the left side of the character
On the right side of the character
options.misconception: confuses meaning radical with phonetic component

options.text: At the bottom of the character
options.misconception: misstates typical radical position

options.text: At the top of the character
options.misconception: misstates typical radical position

questions.explanation: The semantic radical commonly appears on the left side, while the phonetic component often appears on the right. The other positions are less typical for the meaning radical.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.stem: Two characters share the same pronunciation. How do you decide which one to write?

options.text: Use the surrounding context and meaning
Choose randomly since sound is identical
options.misconception: ignores meaning in homophone choice

options.text: Always pick the simpler stroke count
options.misconception: stroke count alone does not determine meaning

options.text: Always pick the one learned first
options.misconception: order learned does not determine correct usage

questions.explanation: Homophones are distinguished by context and intended meaning, not by stroke count or learning order. Random choice would frequently be wrong.
questions.hint: What resolves identical sounds?

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.stem: When writing a character, which stroke is generally written first?

options.text: Top to bottom and left to right
Bottom to top and right to left
options.misconception: reverses standard stroke order

options.text: Inside to outside always
options.misconception: misstates the general rule

options.text: Smallest stroke first
options.misconception: size does not determine order

questions.explanation: Standard stroke order goes top to bottom and left to right. Reversing this or ordering by size or enclosure is not the general rule.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.stem: What is the basic word order in a simple Chinese sentence?

options.text: Subject then verb then object
Verb then subject then object
options.misconception: reverses subject and verb

options.text: Object then subject then verb
options.misconception: reverses object and subject

options.text: Subject then object then verb
options.misconception: places object before verb

questions.explanation: Basic Chinese order is subject-verb-object. The other orders do not match the standard simple sentence pattern.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.stem: Where does a time expression usually go in a Chinese sentence?

options.text: Before the verb and after the subject
After the object at the end
options.misconception: places time too late in sentence

options.text: Before the subject always
options.misconception: places time before subject incorrectly

options.text: Between verb and object
options.misconception: splits verb phrase with time

questions.explanation: Time expressions typically follow the subject and precede the verb. Placing them after the object or between verb and object is ungrammatical.
questions.hint: Time comes before the action.

questions.stem: Which negation word is used for completed actions or possession?

options.text: mei is used for completed actions and possession
bu is used for completed actions and possession
options.misconception: confuses bu with mei usage

options.text: dou is used for completed actions and possession
options.misconception: dou is not a negation word

options.text: ye is used for completed actions and possession
options.misconception: ye is not a negation word

questions.explanation: mei negates completed actions and possession, while bu negates present or future states and habits. dou and ye are not negation words.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.stem: Which particle turns a statement into a yes-no question?

options.text: ma at the end of the sentence
de at the end of the sentence

options.text: le at the end of the sentence
options.misconception: le marks completed action not questions

options.text: guo at the end of the sentence

questions.explanation: ma is the question particle placed at the end of a statement to make it a yes-no question. de, le, and guo serve other grammatical roles.

questions.stem: In Chinese, a number before a noun usually requires what between them?

options.misconception: plural suffix alone is insufficient

options.text: Nothing between number and noun
options.misconception: omits required measure word

questions.explanation: A measure word classifier is required between a number and a noun. Omitting it or using an adjective ending is ungrammatical.

A gao bi B

A habitual action

options.text: A negated action
options.misconception: confuses completed with negation

After the object at the end

options.misconception: places location before subject

options.text: Between verb and object
options.misconception: splits verb phrase with location

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.stem: Where does the adverb hen usually go relative to the adjective?

options.text: Immediately before the adjective
After the adjective
options.misconception: places adverb after adjective

options.text: Before the subject
options.misconception: places adverb before subject

options.text: At the end of the sentence
options.misconception: places adverb at sentence end

questions.explanation: hen and similar adverbs precede the adjective they modify. Placing them after the adjective or elsewhere is ungrammatical.
